 JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Girish S. Hiremath, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri.S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

Claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded in MVC No.151/2009 dated 11.08.2011 on the file Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Vehicle Claims Tribunal,
Haveri.

entities.text:
Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Vehicle Claims Tribunal,
Haveri
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
Claimant being the injured in a road traffic accident that occurred on 25.02.2008 at about 07.45 p.m. at Guttal-kuragunda road, near Gaddi Kariyamma Temple,
involving a tracker bearing No.KA-27/T-9069 and Bajaj Auto Rickshaw bearing No.KA-25/C-761, laid a claim for awarding suitable compensation.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3651 4.
Wound certificate which is marked at Ex.P.5 shows that fracture of clavicle and one simple injury.
5. Claim petition was resisted by filing necessary written statement including the liability of the Insurance Company.

6. Claim petition, on contest, came to be allowed in a sum of Rs.15,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realisation and fastened the liability on the owner of the Bajaj Auto Rickshaw.
7. Being aggrieved by the same, claimant is in appeal.
Basavaraj S/O. Madivalappa Madiwalar vs Bhirappa S/O. Hanamappa Kotihal on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73833293/
2 8. Sri

.Girish S. Hiremath, learned counsel for the appellant, reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum sought for enhanced compensation on the ground that the Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding a meager compensation, even though claimant has sustained a fracture injury.
So also Tribunal has erred in NC: 2024:KHC-D:3651 not properly appreciating the material evidence in fastening the liability on the owner of the vehicle.
9. Per contra, Sri.S.K.Kayakamath, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company supported the impugned judgment.
10. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
11. On such perusal of the material on record, the claimant is successful in establishing that he suffered injuries mentioned in Ex.P.5 in a road traffic accident as aforesaid.
12. Now the question of quantum of compensation is concerned, since there is a fracture injury, he must be awarded minimum of Rs.25,000/- on the head of pain and suffering.
13. Taking note of the fracture injury and yet another simple injury, enhancing the compensation by NC: 2024:KHC-D:3651 Rs.20,000/- in all Rs.35,000/-, would meet the ends of justice.
14. Taking note of the fact that the offending vehicle was duly insured, the liability is to be shifted on to the Insurance Company of the offending vehicle.

15. Accordingly, following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed as against sum of Rs.15,000/- claimant is entitled to Rs.35,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation payable by respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
(ii) Insurance Company is granted four weeks' time to pay the compensation.

Sd/-
